The PKGBUILD defines standard sources: a LICENSE file and prebuilt `.deb` binaries for x86_64 and aarch64, all fetched over HTTPS from the project's official GitHub repository (`stablyai/orca`). The URLs are constructed using `pkgver`, which is statically defined as `1.4.188`. There is no dynamic fetching of `pkgver` via command substitution or network calls — it is hardcoded.

The only executable code at global scope involves setting `_relurl` using string interpolation; this performs no command execution or external communication. There is no `pkgver()` function, so no version-detection logic runs during sourcing. All checksums are present (including per-architecture), and while their presence doesn't affect safety in this context, it confirms source integrity will be verified later.

No code is executed during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` beyond sourcing the PKGBUILD and downloading the sources. The download targets are predictable, static URLs tied directly to a tagged release. No `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` steps are run under these flags, so even the `bsdtar` extraction and `chmod 4755` on the sandbox binary are deferred and irrelevant for this gate.

Thus, simply sourcing the PKGBUILD and fetching the sources poses no risk of remote code execution, data exfiltration, or unintended side effects.
</details>
<summary>
Safe sourcing and downloads from trusted upstream
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The package adheres to typical AUR packaging conventions for `-bin` packages: it avoids stripping binaries (required for Electron), skips debug info, and provides proper licensing. There is no evidence of malicious behavior such as data exfiltration, code injection, or execution of remote scripts. The actions taken are consistent with safely repackaging a trusted upstream binary for Arch Linux.
